text: Optical flow is apparent pixel motion between images caused by scene objects or camera movement. It is not calibrated running speed and does not establish fatigue or terrain semantics.
A stop candidate combines recorded speed below 0.4 m/s with low video motion for at least two seconds. A stationary camera alone cannot prove the runner stopped. Review the clip.

Video time zero corresponds to workout elapsed offset_s. Match a known event in both recordings. Check another event near the end for drift. Missing observations remain missing outside the sample tolerance.
HealthKit workout routes contain timestamped positions. Health data export is XML. Availability of heart rate and running speed varies by recording. A GPX file may omit heart rate.

Camera and speed disagreement is unresolved evidence. A moving camera with near-zero recorded speed may indicate GPS error, clock offset, camera handling, or other movement. No single cause is established.
Future visual scene summaries require a vision model and manually reviewed clips. Current OpenCV measurements do not recognize rocks, stairs, aid stations, injuries, or athlete identity.

Future optimization suggestions should combine verified visual observations, recorded workout data, conditions and athlete goals, then state uncertainty and invite athlete or coach review. Do not infer medical causes from these inputs.
Raw video, exact coordinates and health records remain local by default. Cloud synthesis is opt-in and receives only redacted aggregate evidence. Public reports omit raw records and raw questions.

RaceTime accepts compatible CSV/GPX exports from sports watches such as Garmin, COROS, Suunto and Apple Watch. Apple Health XML is optional. It does not connect to watch accounts or parse FIT/TCX directly. Available metrics depend on the device, sensor and export.

Heart-rate zones require explicit personal boundaries. A sustained zone change highlights a moment to inspect in the video. It does not prove a climb, fatigue or another physiological cause. The bundled thresholds are illustrative.

Core temperature needs an explicit core-temperature field and external sensor provenance. Skin and ambient temperature are different signals and are never substituted. Intermittent SpO2 samples are timestamped; an earlier sample is not a current reading. Neither signal establishes heat strain, a diagnosis or oxygen-limited performance.

The performance brief compares first valid heart rate with the first later peak and other readings at those moments. It proposes an experiment for human review, such as comparing steadier effort on a similar segment with comparable conditions. Measure segment time, intended-zone time, perceived effort and video across repeated sessions; no gain or personalized target is guaranteed.
